fixes.explanation: Pethor by the Euphrates, yes. The text says Balak sent messengers to summon Balaam at Pethor, “…which is by the Euphrates in the land of his people.” (Numbers 22:5) Balak doesn't send a note. He sends a whole delegation. That's the kind of summons you can't leave on read.

Bethel's a real place in the Bible, friend, but it's the wrong address for this delegation. The text puts Balaam at Pethor, “…which is by the Euphrates in the land of his people.” (Numbers 22:5) Balak wants this man badly. He says, “…I know that those you bless are blessed, and those you curse are cursed.” (Numbers 22:6) Send the messengers to the wrong town and the king's whole plan is stuck at the first turn.

That would be dramatic, but it isn't in the text. When the donkey sees the angel of the LORD, “…she turned off the path and went into a field.” (Numbers 22:23) She doesn't toss anybody. She just steers away from that drawn sword. Then Balaam beats her to return her to the path.

Not the staff, friend. Balaam uses that on the donkey, and the LORD answers by giving her a voice. The text says, “Then the LORD opened the donkey’s mouth…” (Numbers 22:28) Her first words are, “What have I done to you that you have beaten me these three times?” Three beatings in, she finally gets to file her complaint.

No storm, friend. Nothing in the sky changes on that road. The surprise is that the donkey has something to say. The text says, “Then the LORD opened the donkey’s mouth…” (Numbers 22:28) Picture being the man who just got asked “What have I done to you…” by his own ride. I'd have no answer ready.

Sinned is right, baker. Balaam bows low and falls facedown (Numbers 22:31). The angel of the LORD asks why he has beaten his donkey, and then Balaam answers, “I have sinned…” (Numbers 22:34) He goes on, “for I did not realize that you were standing in the road to confront me.” Earlier he told the donkey he'd kill her if he had a sword (Numbers 22:29). Now he's the one owning up.

Not this time, friend. Balaam bows low and falls facedown, and the angel of the LORD asks why he has beaten his donkey these three times (Numbers 22:31, 32). Only then does Balaam answer, “I have sinned…” (Numbers 22:34) It's a short, honest line, and it comes after the angel speaks.
